methods.evidence: Negotiates this connection's protocol version and client capabilities, so it decides what the connection may afterwards be asked to do
Selects the authentication method this connection acts under and starts the vendor's own credential flow; the credential stays with the agent and never reaches a component
Creates an execution the agent owns, with its working directory and its MCP servers
Loads a stored conversation into this connection; stored history is not evidence that this process owns the live execution
Submits a turn with its content blocks, which is what makes the agent act
Changes the session's approval mode, which alters what the agent runs without asking
Changes the model the session's next turn uses

Ends the turn in flight. The name is in the installed executable; sent as a request this build answers method not found, which is what a notification-only handler does, and it was not exercised as a notification
Carries the agent's own stream of turn updates: message and reasoning chunks, tool calls and their results, plans and the available command list
A reverse request naming the tool call the agent is waiting on and the options it offers; answering it runs or refuses that call, so it is not a report
Reads a file and returns its text. It changes nothing, and it must run in the selected host environment under that environment's own identity rather than wherever a client happens to be
Writes a file in the selected host environment under that environment's own identity
Starts a process in the selected host environment with the broker's scoped resources; it is not a read
Reads what a terminal the agent created has produced so far
Waits for a terminal the agent created and reports how it ended
Releases a terminal and the resources the broker scoped to it

qualification_note: Qualified against Gemini CLI 0.60.0 (npm @google/gemini-cli) on 2026-09-20 by starting that build with --acp and reading what it answered over its standard streams: ACP protocol version 1, agentInfo gemini-cli 0.60.0, and prompt capabilities for image, audio and embedded context. Each host-to-upstream method here was sent to that build and answered; each upstream-to-host method is a name present in that build's own files. ACP is an explicitly selected mode that creates its own execution: it is not the stock terminal, and nothing here attaches it to a live terminal conversation. max_message_bytes is this host's bound, not a vendor limit. Volatile forwarding is untested. fixtures/frames.json pins the evidence and docs/qualification-notes.md records what each claim was checked against.
